subject: Post-call recap & ops capture — Emberline inference requirements

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call recap & ops capture — Emberline inference requirements

Sara — thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Key pain / goals we captured
- Current infra: Emberline is running a hybrid service for document summarization (internal UI + API) with a single model variant; spikes during nightly batch jobs and peak business-hours traffic (09:30–11:30 PT).
- Pain: token cost is dominating unit economics + 95th-latency spikes causing UI timeouts for agents.
- Goal: reduce 95th percentile latency to <= 180ms for 1–2k concurrent users (approx 20 TPS sustained, burst to 80 TPS), while cutting per-inference token cost by ~30%.

Concrete workload signals you shared (please correct if I mis-stated)
- Avg payload: 120 tokens request, 900 tokens response (single-step summarization).
- Baseline traffic: 20 TPS sustained, peak bursts 80 TPS for ~10m windows.
- Latency target: 95p <= 180ms end-to-end for interactive flows.
- Tolerance for model-change: must preserve top-1 relevancy for legal/QA use cases; regressions >2% F1 are blockers.

Immediate implications (ops & topology)
- We should prioritize: (1) KV/prefix caching for repeated document context, (2) batching policy tuned for tail latency, (3) model quantization (int8) candidate for non-critical inference paths.
- Initial capacity sketch: 2 x A100-equivalent GPUs with autoscale burst to 4 for peak windows OR Redwood Dedicated with reserved pool + hosted fallback.

Requested artifacts attached: Emberline production metrics export (you provided) and our topology sketch from today.

Next steps
1) Marissa to propose a concise topology (instance sizes, batching config, cache TTLs) by EOD tomorrow.
2) David to share a short cost/latency estimate comparing: Dedicated reserved 2-GPU pool vs Hosted with autoscale burst.
3) Emberline to run the sample trace we shared and return a 1-hour harvest of 95p latency during a simulated burst (if possible).

If anything above is off, reply inline and we’ll update. Happy to set a follow-up tech deep-dive next week (we penciled Fri 08/02 10:00 PT).

—
David Kim
Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference

Sara — appreciate the clarity. Quick technical sketch and assumptions so procurement and engineering have a concrete starting point.

Assumptions from metrics provided
- Median request: 120 tokens in / 520 tokens out.
- Peak concurrent request rate: ~80 TPS for ~10 minutes.
- Target 95p latency budget: 180ms (client-side).

Recommended topology (short)
- Primary: Redwood Dedicated — 2 x A100-40GB (reserved pool) with continuous batching tuned to 20ms max batch walltime, per-device concurrency configured to maintain tail latency.
- Burst / fallback: Hosted pool with rtx6000-equivalent nodes that can scale to add 2 GPUs for short windows. Routing policy: prefer Dedicated -> if queue > 200 requests or CPU memory saturation then overflow to Hosted pool with model-variant matched to avoid cold-cache penalty.
- Model variant & execution: move to a quantized int8 build of the chosen 20B family for non-legal-critical paths; keep fp16 for canonical legal checks (sample 10% of responses for verification).
- Caching: prefix/KV cache with 30–45 minute TTL for repeated document context; expect ~25–35% token reuse in daily workloads based on your traces.

Performance & cost sketch (very high level)
- With above: expected median latency ~90–120ms, 95p ~150–175ms with tuned batching and KV reuse.
- Token cost reduction estimate: 20–35% using int8 + cache reuse (depends on acceptance test pass-rates).

Operational notes
- Rollout plan: start with a canary (5% traffic) on quantized variant + automated eval suite; rollback if top-1 relevancy delta >2% on acceptance prompts.
- Observability: enable token-level traces and per-route 95p dashboards; we'll add an alert when 95p exceeds 210ms for >5m.

Attachments: redwood-topology-sketch.pdf contains a driven diagram with batching windows, KV cache placement, and routing policy.

Would you like Karthik or I to join a follow-up with your infra/eng team to walk the sketch and answer deeper questions about cache consistency and routing semantics?

—
Marissa Cole
Sr Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
